medDays.title: Medication days
medDays.what: A medication day is a day you took acute (attack) medication – triptans, painkillers or combinations. Migrano counts days, not pills.
medDays.why: Taking acute medication on 10 or more days a month (15 for simple painkillers) for three months can itself cause headache – doctors call it medication-overuse headache. The count helps you notice early and talk to your doctor in time.
medDays.limitHint: Change it under Settings. Migrano only counts and tells you when you reach it.
medDays.disclaimer: This is not a diagnosis. Never stop or change medication without talking to your doctor.

weather.title: Air pressure
weather.hint: Track daily air pressure for your place – no location access needed.
weather.pickHint: Type a city or town. Only its coordinates are sent to the weather service (Open-Meteo) – never your device location.
weather.privacy: Open-Meteo is a free, open weather service without accounts or tracking. The pressure history is stored on your device only.
weather.infoWhat: Air pressure (hPa) is the weight of the atmosphere. Around 1013 hPa is average; rising pressure usually means settled weather, falling pressure means a front is coming.
weather.infoWhy: Many people with migraine report attacks when the pressure drops quickly (a fall of 5 hPa or more within a day), but studies disagree and the effect differs from person to person. The absolute value matters less than the change.
weather.infoApp: Migrano stores the daily mean for your place and compares the days your attacks started with all other days. The pattern card and the doctor's report show that comparison – nothing more.
weather.infoDisclaimer: This is a description of your own log, not a medical statement. Talk to your doctor about what it means for you.
